title: Implement graceful control-plane subnet draining and DNS switchover
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context and motivation: customers running Redwood Private have reported intermittent control-plane connectivity during upgrades that reassign control-plane endpoints across subnets (especially in multi-AZ installs with cross-account privatelink). This PR adds a controlled subnet-draining workflow plus an atomic DNS switchover mechanism to ensure in-flight requests are not dropped and delegation/zone records remain intact.

Goals: 1) Allow operators to mark a control-plane subnet as DRAINING to move control-plane endpoints and cleanup ENI bindings without service interruption. 2) Provide a deterministic DNS switchover that preserves authoritative records, respects TTLs, and records a reversible migration path. 3) Integrate changes into Terraform modules, the installer Helm charts, and the upgrade/rollback operator so rollouts can be canaried and aborted safely.

What this PR includes: Terraform module changes (modules/network): - subnet lifecycle flag (control_plane_subnet.lifecycle = "managed|standby|draining") - new resource aws_subnet_drain_provisioner (idempotent Lambda invoked by lifecycle hooks) - route-table reconciliation to prevent blackhole routes during transition - new outputs: draining_state, last_drain_timestamp Installer Helm chart updates (charts/private-controlplane): - control-plane-sidecar: subnet-prober and dns-switchover-controller containers - configmaps for TTL policy and switchover window - CRD change: ControlPlaneSubnet CRD gains .spec.lifecycle and .status.drainProgress Upgrade operator and rollback tooling: - introduce canary windows by AZ and region, automated health checks that evaluate: API responsiveness, KV cache warmup, ENI count deltas, and DNS propagation status - safe-abort: rollback rebind procedure that attempts to promote previous control-plane ENIs and reapply previous Route53 records DNS handling and safety: - staged switchover writes: create new A/AAAA and alias records in a 'staged' state, wait for health checks and low TTL expiry, then atomically swap by updating Route53 change-sets and handing over delegation metadata. Includes safeguards for cross-account zone delegations and resolver rules (Route53 Resolver): if delegation targets differ, we perform a conditional delegation update with audit entry.

Rollback plan: the operator keeps the previous control-plane records for a configurable retention window. If any critical health check fails during the canary, the operator triggers safe-abort which reverses DNS changes and reassigns ENIs back to origin subnets where possible.

Testing and QA: - Unit tests for Terraform module (plan-time idempotency simulated) - Integration harness test running a multi-AZ scenario on a pruning environment that asserts no 5xx spikes during a drain + switchover - E2E test that exercises failure injection: drop cross-AZ peering then verify safe-abort path - Added Prometheus metrics (controlplane_subnet_drain_progress, dns_switchover_phase) and Grafana dashboard snippets for rollout visibility

Migration notes: existing installs are unaffected until operators set .spec.lifecycle to "draining". The default lifecycle remains "managed". For air-gapped installs we provide a no-op dns-switchover-controller mode (dry-run) to allow offline validation.

Related: ENG-1245 (subnet lifecycle API), ENG-1307 (dns switchover design), SUP-4521 (customer incident that motivated canary behavior).

release_notes: Adds a controlled subnet draining workflow and DNS switchover procedure for control-plane migrations. Operator can now mark control-plane subnets as 'draining' to safely reassign ENIs and perform an atomic DNS handoff. Integrates Terraform module changes, Helm charts, and upgrade operator canaries. Backward compatible unless lifecycle=draining is used.
